issues.description: The problem statement UML specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (an int return type), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and introduces a new StudentCount class that is not present or mentioned in the problem statement or the template. This mismatch in the method return type (and the addition of a new helper class) is a structural inconsistency that would confuse students and make it unclear whether they should return an int or a StudentCount.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of getTotalNumberOfStudents consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove the StudentCount class, updating all callers accordingly. Alternatively, if StudentCount is intended as part of the design, update the problem statement UML and the template to declare and describe StudentCount and change the UML to show getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount so students know to implement/use that class.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (a primitive int representing the total number of students), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and also introduces a new StudentCount class. This represents the same conceptual entity (the total number of students) with a different identifier/type across artifacts and can confuse students who expect to work with an int as specified in the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the total number of students across artifacts. Preferably change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (primitive) as specified in the UML and remove the StudentCount wrapper class, or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to explicitly define and document the StudentCount type if a wrapper is pedagogically intended. This ensures a single, consistent identifier/type for the same concept.
